extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for ACL Rolling Review (ACL/ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation form for reviewers assessing submissions to the ACL Rolling Review; covers summary, strengths/weaknesses, numeric ratings (confidence, soundness, excitement, overall), and specific assessments (ethics, reproducibility, datasets, software, author identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers describe the paper's subject matter to ensure understanding and identify potential misinterpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary that demonstrates the reviewer's understanding of the submission; used to catch misinterpretations and confirm the reviewer read the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify publication reasons including novel methodology, empirical results, theoretical analysis, and literature organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the paper's main positive contributions (e.g., novelty in method, strong empirical evidence, valuable theoretical insight, or useful survey/organization of literature) that justify acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail concerns about correctness, limited impact, clarity issues, or other factors that might deprioritize the paper among competing submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain substantive technical or empirical problems (e.g., correctness issues, insufficient evidence, limited significance), clarity or presentation issues, or other reasons the paper should be ranked lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments/Suggestions/Typos
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive feedback for author improvements beyond addressing major concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable suggestions, minor corrections, and copyediting notes (typos/formatting) to help authors improve the manuscript; focus on constructive, concrete advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Confidence (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessed confidence in the review on a 1–5 scale reflecting familiarity with related work and thoroughness of checking important points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale definitions: 5 = Positive evaluation; careful reading with familiarity of related work. 4 = Quite sure; important points checked carefully. 3 = Pretty sure; general area knowledge but incomplete detail verification. 2 = Willing to defend evaluation; likely missed details or novelty concerns. 1 = Outside expertise area or paper very difficult to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness (1-5 scale, half-point options allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the technical/methodological soundness and sufficiency of evidence supporting the main claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale guidance: 5 = Exemplary thoroughness for paper type. 4 = Sufficient support for claims; minor experiments could enhance. 3 = Adequate main claim support; minor points need strengthening. 2 = Main claims lack sufficient support; major technical/methodological issues. 1 = Insufficient for publication or irrelevant to ACL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excitement (1-5 scale, half-point options allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective assessment of transformational potential, community impact, or personal research relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale guidance: 5 = Highly exciting; would recommend to others. 4 = Exciting; would mention to colleagues. 3 = Interesting; might attend presentation. 2 = Potentially interesting; may resonate with others. 1 = Not exciting; lacks computational linguistics relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Assessment (1-5 scale, half-point options allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate recommendation for acceptance/resubmission/award placement based on the reviewer's judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale guidance: 5 = Consider for Award (top 2.5%). 4 = Conference acceptance. 3 = Findings acceptance. 2 = Resubmit next cycle with revisions. 1 = Do not resubmit or not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Paper Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Required justification when recommending a paper for award-level consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When giving an award-level (5) overall assessment, provide explicit justification explaining why the paper merits top-tier recognition relative to other submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations & Societal Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of author acknowledgment regarding potential harms, bias, exclusion, and dual-use concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the authors discuss limitations and potential societal impacts (harms, biases, exclusion, dual-use). Note unacknowledged risks or missing mitigation strategies; comment on adequacy of authors' discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the submission for ethical issues in accordance with the ACL Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any ethical problems (data collection, privacy, harmful applications, misrepresentation). Evaluate against ACL Code of Ethics and flag concerns that may require further scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Review Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether an in-depth ethics committee review is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State yes/no (or equivalent) on whether the paper should be referred to the ethics committee for deeper evaluation based on identified concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess availability of parameters, data, and methodological clarity to enable reproduction of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate how well the paper provides necessary artifacts and descriptions (code, datasets, training details, hyperparameters) and whether the methods are described with sufficient clarity for reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the value of any newly released dataset from enabling to documentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider novelty, usefulness, documentation, licensing, and ethical considerations of released datasets. Scale ranges from highly enabling datasets to those that are primarily documentary or of limited utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the utility and value of any newly released software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate usability, completeness, documentation, and potential for community adoption; consider whether the software substantively enables reproduction or further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Identity Knowledge (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any identifying information sources and the reviewer's knowledge of the authors' identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate and describe the extent to which the reviewer knows or has inferred the authors' identities (e.g., recognized writing, cited works, arXiv posting), for transparency in single/double-blind review contexts.
